transcript.answer:
Collection: Each Lore service records OpenTelemetry metrics and serves them as Prometheus text on a dedicated `metrics` port. The default is 9464, set with `LORE_METRICS_PORT`, and it uses `@opentelemetry/exporter-prometheus`. lore-api hands the Prometheus reader to its NodeSDK. Traces still go to Cloud Trace. The stations service and the lore-mcp gateway each register their own MeterProvider. The Cloud Monitoring metric exporter is gone. All Lore instruments are defined in `libs/shared/src/outbound/otel/metrics.ts`. They are resolved lazily against the current global meter provider, and each metric is recorded at exactly one site. Examples are `lore.station.runs`, `lore.station.duration_ms`, `lore.bus.deliveries`, `lore.bus.queue_depth`, `lore.http.requests`, `lore.http.duration_ms`, `lore.llm.*`, and the `lore.billed.cost_usd` gauge. The floor and the agent controller keep their own `/metrics` endpoints, and those are scraped as they are. The Helm Services expose the `metrics` port.

Scraping: Terraform installs kube-prometheus-stack in a `monitoring` namespace when `enable_monitoring` is on. It has PodMonitors and ServiceMonitors for every service, and node-exporter and the GKE-hidden control-plane targets are off.

Viewing: Grafana (at grafana.gcp.re-cinq.com) sits behind oauth2-proxy using the same Google client as Headlamp. It has five dashboards: factory overview, assembly line, agent controller, services, and spend. The assembly-line board is a single dashboard whose `line` variable is read from metric labels, so new lines appear on their own. The web UI links to Grafana only if terraform supplies `GRAFANA_URL`.

judgements.reason: The answer covers OpenTelemetry metrics served as Prometheus text on port 9464, scraping by kube-prometheus-stack via terraform enable_monitoring, Grafana for viewing, and traces to Cloud Trace in the lore-api context, with no contradictions.
